Let me hear your story, what religion you came from, and what was the moment you realized you were Atheist.

My story isn't exciting at all, it was more of a realization that I never really believed in a god. My "belief" was more of a fear of doubting what I had been told my whole life. I was raised christian in a small southern town, where I didn't even know people didn't believe in a god until I was a teenager. It was just unheard of.

I had always wondered how a god could let so much suffering go on in the world, and be part of "his plan". It wasn't until I worked with a minister at my last job that I finally realized I was atheist. I had questions he couldn't answer, and didn't understand why I would ask them in the first place if I "had faith".

My wife and I both came to the realization at the same time, as we had always had the same feeling about religion and were raised similarly. I honestly don't think that I ever truly thought there was a higher being, but actually overcoming the fear of doubting it was my breaking point, and I finally called myself atheist.

I live in the south and I do not hide what I feel, and yes that causes plenty of controversy, but I make sure to only talk about it when asked. Both of my parents know that I am atheist, and my father respects my wishes. My mother on the other hand just thinks it is like I am on "vacation" from religion to act on some urges or something. She will never truly understand. I think my dad is curious though, as he asks me questions about it.

I am very glad I never came to the realization while I lived in my family home, as I fear I would have been disowned and kicked out.

So, why are you here?
